title:
Student life.
Organized.
subtitle: Student Management Dashboard
body: A shared place for clubs, activities and participation.
note: Introduce this as a club and extracurricular management project. It serves students, student club owners and teachers. The screenshots use fictional demonstration data.

title: One connected school experience
subtitle: Bring the steps around an activity into one place.
cards: Students need a clear way to find clubs and upcoming activities.
Club owners need registrations, member lists and attendance together.
Teachers need visibility into applications, participation and council teams.
takeaway: The project connects discovery, organization and reflection.
note: Frame these as needs the project addresses, not a measured claim about a specific school's current processes.

title: Three perspectives. Clear responsibilities.
subtitle: Club ownership is a responsibility within the student role.
cards: Browse and join clubs. Register for activities. Read journals and share feedback.
Manage owned clubs, plan activities, record attendance and publish journals.
Review club applications, organize official events and manage student council years.
takeaway: The original internal teacher role is named “founder”; student club founders stay students.
note: There are two account roles: student and founder. The founder role means teacher. Club owner authorization depends on the student's ownership of a specific club.

title: From an idea to a shared memory
subtitle: A complete journey around a school club.
takeaway: Notifications connect the people involved at each stage.
note: Club applications are reviewed directly by teachers. Election services exist in the backend but are not part of this rendered workflow.

title: A useful starting point
subtitle: See clubs, registrations and community activity at a glance.
points: Dashboard summaries come from stored application data.
Club and activity links lead into the next action.
Language and theme controls support the existing interface.
note: The student dashboard includes club information, participation summaries and rankings. Teachers see their own management board at the same home route.

title: Find a club. Find your people.
subtitle: Browse categories and open a club to explore its activities.
points: Explore clubs and organizations by category.
Join or leave ordinary clubs from the interface.
Official organization membership is managed by teachers.
note: Joining a club and registering for a specific activity are distinct operations. Founders must remain members of their own clubs.

title: Make participation straightforward
subtitle: View an activity, register, then find it in My Registrations.
points: View upcoming and past activities for a club.
Registration checks available capacity and whether the activity is open.
My Registrations brings a student's bookings together.
note: Registration is stored on the server. The UI supports unregistering through the club page and My Registrations. The backend enforces student identity, capacity and activity status.

title: Turn a club idea into a proposal
subtitle: A structured application connects students with teacher review.
points: Provide club details, category and founder names.
Official-club requests also identify a managing teacher.
Track the decision and read the teacher's feedback.
note: The pictured example shows a rejected application and feedback. Approval establishes the club directly; rejection requires a teacher comment.

title: One place to run a club
subtitle: Owned-club tools separate member work from activity planning.
points: Open member rosters and weekly check-in.
Add and edit activities for an owned club.
Cancel upcoming activities with a participant message.
note: Club management is restricted to the owning student. An owner of one club cannot manage another club. Cancellation hides the activity from current views while retaining metadata on the server.

title: Record attendance by week
subtitle: A calendar view turns participation into a usable record.
points: Choose a week and mark present, absent or leave.
Records belong to a club, student and week.
Three present sessions help determine rating eligibility.
note: The current product permits owner-entered attendance, including the owner's own attendance. There is no teacher-approval workflow. Week keys follow local calendar Mondays.

title: Give each activity a story
subtitle: Publish reflections, participants, photos and a social link.
points: Club owners create and edit the activity journal.
Authenticated users can view published journals.
Likes, rated comments and replies keep the conversation going.
note: Journal editing supports up to eight supported images and selecting registered participants. Published photos are served through authenticated API routes. Authors can delete their own comment trees.

title: Feedback grounded in participation
subtitle: Club ratings combine attendance eligibility with community feedback.
points: Students must be members with three present sessions to rate.
Ratings cover four dimensions plus an overall score.
Students can update their rating; teachers can review summaries.
note: Ratings are stored per student and club and can be updated. Named community feedback is visible within the authenticated application. Three present sessions and current membership are required before rating.

title: Support clubs with clear decisions
subtitle: The teacher home page brings applications and school activity together.
points: Review pending club applications.
Approve a club or reject it with a reason.
Applicants receive the result and feedback.
note: The teacher role is internally named founder. This is a separate rendering of the home route, not a third account role. Decisions are stored and the applicant receives a notification.

title: Coordinate official school activity
subtitle: Teachers publish official events and review participation.
points: Create official events using the activity form.
View students registered for each event.
Review club attendance and rating summaries.
note: Teachers can also manage membership in the School Official Events category. The roster includes the details needed for teacher management.

title: Keep council years connected
subtitle: Create a new team while preserving earlier council terms.
points: Set the school year and departments.
Search and select students for the new crew.
Archive the previous term and inspect its details later.
note: Starting a council term replaces current council membership with the new departments' union and archives the previous term. The original UI has no standalone department assign/remove screen.

title: Close the loop with notifications
subtitle: Updates appear where people can act on them.
points: Application decisions return to the applicant.
Registrations and journal interactions inform the relevant people.
Cancellation notices preserve the message for participants.
note: This screenshot is from a captured workflow state, rather than a separate route. Read status and notification lists are scoped to the signed-in recipient.

title: A shared UI. A persistent backend.
subtitle: A TypeScript monorepo connects the screens to stored data.
cards: Users, clubs, activities, records and photos
takeaway: The server checks identity and permissions before saving a command in a transaction.
note: The frontend reads /api/state and sends /api/commands; Better Auth handles /api/auth/*. Writes use a transaction with a project-specific advisory lock. Core relationships use relational tables; complex records use separate typed JSONB tables.

title: Make the records dependable
subtitle: Checks live alongside the data and workflows.
cards: Better Auth sessions identify the user. Teacher and owner permissions are checked by the server.
Shared Zod contracts check command inputs and responses. Capacity, attendance and journal rules are enforced.
PostgreSQL stores business data and journal photos. Transactions keep connected writes together.
takeaway: Students receive scoped data; roster contact access depends on role and ownership.
note: Do not describe this as a production security certification. The aggregate state loading and serialized writes fit the current small application; larger deployments would need additional scalability work.

title: Show the product as it exists
subtitle: Visible workflows and backend-only services are distinct.
cards: Clubs, applications, activities, registrations, attendance, journals, feedback, official events, council years and notifications.
Club and event election services exist, but election links redirect to Clubs. There is no rendered election or scoring screen.
takeaway: Screenshot evidence demonstrates captured interface states. Test results are reported separately in the project handoff.
note: The existing docs/action-inventory.json lists 31 commands. Some are dormant. Do not equate action count with reachable pages or describe all tests as passed while final verification is running.

title:
Discover. Participate.
Organize. Reflect.
subtitle: One connected workflow for extracurricular life.
body: Students take part. Club owners coordinate. Teachers support and oversee.
takeaway: Explore the page gallery next, or open the dashboard for a live walkthrough.
note: The appendix contains the captured route and role views. All screenshots use fictional demonstration data. The presentation itself is a standalone local artifact.
